# Test fixtures

Small, curated, committed inputs. Large recordings belong in `recordings/` (git-ignored).

- `measurement_bearing_only_v1.hex`: golden wire frame (v1), derived by hand from
  the format spec, not produced by either encoder. Both the C++ and Python tests
  must reproduce it exactly. If it has to change, the wire version changes too.
- `scenarios/<name>/`: ground-truth regression scenarios generated by the simulator
  (`sim/sifted_sim/scenarios.py`):
  - `sensors.cfg`: sensor table (ADR 0003)
  - `frames.hex`: one wire-v1 frame per line, hex, in send order (multi-sensor
    scenarios: all sensors merged in time order)
  - `truth.csv`, in one of two layouts told apart by the header:
    - `time_ns,x_m,y_m,vx_mps,vy_mps`: single target (M1), one row per frame.
      Used by `tests/scenario_regression_test.cpp` (`straight_crossing`, `turn`).
    - `time_ns,x_m,y_m,vx_mps,vy_mps,target_id,covered`: multi-target (M2), one
      row per (truth time, target) for every target that exists, sorted by time
      then target id; `covered` is 1 when the target is inside the coverage of a
      sensor that can start tracks. Used by
      `tests/multi_target_regression_test.cpp` (`crossing_pair`, `close_pass`,
      `enter_leave`). Rows are truth samples, not frames.

    Layout 2 only appends columns, so M1 readers and fixtures are unaffected.

  Regenerate after changing a scenario or the simulator, then re-check the
  baselines in the regression test headers:

  ```bash
  cd sim && for s in straight_crossing turn crossing_pair close_pass enter_leave; do
    python3 -m sifted_sim.generate $s ../tests/fixtures/scenarios/$s; done
  ```
